_comment: FAST PC News - the LATEST items on About -> PC News
Written nightly by the news sweep step of the daily-intel-watch scheduled task, committed
here on main, and published to fast-updates/intel/ by tools/Publish-IntelFeed.ps1, which
refuses the file if any rule below is broken. FAST also ships this copy and uses whichever
is newer (PcNewsData.Load). PcNewsFileTests pins the same rules on the shipped copy.
THE PAGE IS FREE AND ONLY INFORMS. An item says what happened, who it affects and where it
came from. Whether to install or roll back a driver, and what to do about a Windows update,
is the advice on the paid GPU Drivers and System Score pages, so no item gives it.
FIELDS (every item):
id       - stable, unique, lower-case words and hyphens, e.g. 2026-10-21-nvidia-621-01-black-screens
date     - yyyy-MM-dd the news happened (not the day the sweep found it)
kind     - problem | release
category - problems only: stability (crashes, black screens, freezes, games that will not
start) | performance (FPS, stutter, latency) | security
status   - problems only: confirmed (the vendor, Microsoft or Epic says so) | reported
(at least two independent outlets or threads, no vendor statement yet)
headline - up to 100 characters, FAST's own words
summary  - up to 400 characters, one or two sentences, FAST's own words, consequence first
applies  - tags FAST matches against this PC in code, OR'd: all | gpu:nvidia | gpu:amd |
gpu:intel | gpu-name:<text in the GPU name, e.g. RTX 50> | cpu:intel | cpu:amd |
cpu-name:<text in the CPU name, e.g. i9-14> | game:fortnite | app:obs
sources  - [{ name, url }], https only; a reported problem needs two
expires  - yyyy-MM-dd, no more than 31 days after date
SECURITY ITEMS ALSO HAVE:
audience - who is affected, in plain words; say so when ordinary gaming PCs are not
action   - optional, what to do (update the browser, rotate keys). Security only.
PROBLEMS MAY ALSO HAVE:
fixed_in - optional, what fixes it, copied from the vendor's own page, never worked out:
{ nvidia_driver: one GeForce driver per branch, e.g. [616.56, 610.88],
windows_builds: build.revision per Windows version, e.g. [26100.7019] }.
FAST compares them with the PC in code and says it has the fix or needs it
(PcNews.FixStatus), only where the applies tags match or applies is empty.
RULES: no advice in headline or summary; no em dashes; never name a product as the cause of
someone's problem unless its maker said so; never claim anything works with an anti-cheat;
a single article or a rumour is not news; at most 20 live items.

items.headline: OBS Studio 33.0.2 and 33.0.3 fix a batch of crashes, including a startup crash on some older CPUs
items.summary: OBS Studio 33.0.2 fixes several crashes, including a browser related startup crash and virtual camera crashes on Windows, makes controller input in browser sources keep working when OBS is in the background, and turns on WebGPU for browser sources. 33.0.3, out November 22, fixes the crash at startup on certain older processors that 33.0.2 brought.

items.headline: A new Windows lock screen bypass lets someone holding a locked PC run programs on it
items.summary: Two outlets report that a researcher posted a method on November 19, called FastUnlock, that uses Narrator on the lock screen to run programs in a limited account without signing in, and a security firm says it works. It needs hands on the PC and a Microsoft account on it. Microsoft has not released a fix, and no attacks using it have been reported.
items.audience: Windows PCs signed in with a Microsoft account that a stranger can get their hands on, such as a laptop. Nobody can use it over the internet, so a gaming PC at home is at low risk.
items.action: Keep Windows updated so the fix arrives when Microsoft ships it, and do not leave a laptop where others can reach it.

items.headline: ASUS fixes an Armoury Crate flaw that could let a program on the PC take full control of it
items.summary: ASUS lists Armoury Crate versions up to 6.7.2 as affected by CVE-2026-112115. BleepingComputer reports it as a high-severity flaw that lets a program or user already on the PC without admin rights trick an elevated Armoury Crate process into loading a malicious file and gain full control.
items.audience: PCs with ASUS Armoury Crate 6.7.2 or older installed, which ships with many ASUS motherboards, laptops and ROG devices.
items.action: Update Armoury Crate to its newest version from the app's own update page or from ASUS's site.

items.headline: NVIDIA's beta hotfix 621.35 fixes the nonstop system drive writes seen on drivers 621.14 and 621.24
items.summary: NVIDIA confirmed a bug that can make its display service write to a log file on the system drive nonstop in the background; users reported it on GeForce drivers 621.14 and 621.24, up to 30 GB an hour on some PCs. Beta hotfix 621.35, out November 20, fixes it and is on NVIDIA's site, not in the NVIDIA App. The fix comes in NVIDIA's next WHQL driver, which has no date yet.

items.headline: Chrome 158 fixes 204 security flaws, six of them rated critical
items.summary: Google's November 17 Chrome update for Windows, version 158.0.8127.36/37, fixes 204 security flaws, six rated critical, among them flaws in its graphics, audio and video handling. Google does not say any of them has been used in attacks. Chrome installs the update itself but only finishes it after a restart.
items.audience: Anyone who uses Google Chrome on a PC and has not restarted it since the update arrived.
items.action: Keep your browser updated: open Chrome's menu, Help, About Google Chrome, and select Relaunch if it asks.

items.headline: Hijacked scripts on CNN, BBC, Zoom and other big sites tried to steal card and crypto details
items.summary: Several outlets report that on November 16 an attacker planted code in scripts that Optimizely, a web testing service, delivers to the sites of at least 178 organizations, among them CNN, the BBC and Zoom. The code was built to capture card details typed into those pages and to swap crypto wallet addresses for the attacker's. Optimizely says it fixed the flaw and removed the code.
items.audience: Anyone who typed card details or copied a crypto wallet address on an affected site on November 16. The PC itself is not affected.
items.action: Check your card statement for payments you do not recognise, and check where any crypto transfer made that day went.

items.headline: CapFrameX 1.9.2 adds a tile overlay you can design yourself and a lighter in-game overlay
items.summary: CapFrameX 1.9.2 brings a tile overlay with its own editor and 45 starter designs, says its overlay now takes less from the game, and fixes PresentMon captures in long sessions and with frame generation. It now needs the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime.

items.headline: Public exploit code claims a way to take full control of Windows 11 from an ordinary account
items.summary: Several outlets report that a researcher posted code on November 10 that lets a program already running under a normal account on current Windows 11 gain full SYSTEM control, and the researcher says it can switch off antivirus too. Microsoft says it is investigating and has not released a fix, and no attacks using it have been reported.
items.audience: Windows 11 PCs with Microsoft's log file protection on, which is the default on 25H2 and 26H2. An attacker first needs a program running on the PC.
items.action: Keep Windows and Microsoft Defender updated, and do not run programs from sources you do not trust.

items.headline: November's Microsoft updates fix an Outlook flaw attackers were already using
items.summary: Microsoft says CVE-2026-124194 in Outlook was exploited before its November 10 fix: opening a booby-trapped message file could make Outlook contact an attacker's server without its usual warning and hand over the Windows sign-in hash, which could be used to pose as the user. Opening the file is needed; the preview pane is not enough.
items.audience: Anyone who uses the Outlook desktop app on Windows and has not installed November's Office updates. PCs without Outlook are not affected.
items.action: Keep Office and Windows updated, and do not open message files from people you do not know.

items.headline: November's Windows 11 update brings back USB audio devices that stopped working in September
items.summary: Microsoft says the November 10 update for Windows 11 24H2, 25H2 and 26H2 fixes USB Audio 1.0 devices that failed to start with error code 10 after September's security update, along with this month's security fixes.

items.headline: Discord's November update makes Go Live streaming lighter on the CPU and the app quicker to open
items.summary: Discord says Go Live now copies fewer frames from the GPU to the CPU, cutting its CPU use while streaming by about 4.5 percent, and that the desktop app reaches a usable state noticeably faster than in April.

items.headline: Chrome 157 fixes a browser flaw Google says attackers are already using
items.summary: Google's November 9 Chrome update for Windows, version 157.0.8103.50/51, fixes nine security flaws, and Google says an exploit for one of them, CVE-2026-125350 in Chrome's XML handling, exists in the wild. Chrome installs the update itself but only finishes it after a restart.
items.audience: Anyone who uses Google Chrome on a PC and has not restarted it since the update arrived.
items.action: Keep your browser updated: open Chrome's menu, Help, About Google Chrome, and select Relaunch if it asks.

items.headline: A Windows Paint flaw could let an attacker run code over a network, and its fix comes from the Store
items.summary: Microsoft rates CVE-2026-83844, a flaw in the Paint app, at 8.1 out of 10: an attacker could run code on a PC over a network without signing in, though Microsoft says an attack is hard to pull off and none has been seen. The Hacker News reports the fixed Paint build, 11.2609.401.0, arrives through the Microsoft Store, not Windows Update.
items.audience: Every Windows PC with the Paint app whose copy has not yet updated from the Microsoft Store. Attacks have not been seen.
items.action: Open the Microsoft Store, go to Downloads and select Get updates so Paint installs its newest version.

items.headline: The NIKKE PC launcher was tampered with and served malware to players for weeks
items.summary: Level Infinite says a third party altered script files in the PC launcher for Goddess of Victory: NIKKE, and it shipped a fixed client on November 4. Researchers say the altered files, changed from late September, installed a remote-access tool that can take NIKKE logins, saved browser passwords and crypto wallet data. Only the PC launcher is named; the phone versions are not.
items.audience: Anyone who opened the NIKKE PC launcher from late September to November 4. A PC without NIKKE is not affected.
items.action: Update the NIKKE launcher and run a full antivirus scan. If you played in that window, change your NIKKE, email and browser-saved passwords from another device.

items.headline: NVIDIA's 621.14 driver fixes the 621.01 bug that freezes or blacks out the screen during video
items.summary: NVIDIA confirmed a bug in GeForce driver 621.01 that freezes the screen or turns it black for several seconds while a video plays in Chrome, Edge or VLC, sometimes when a game starts with a video open. Beta hotfix 621.12 fixed it on October 27, and Game Ready driver 621.14, out November 4, carries the fix for RTX 50 cards. The screen recovers without a restart.
